content:
The Spirits’ Book
Published by Allan Kardec in 1857, it is the main book of spiritist philosophy. We can call it its backbone because it supports all other works of Spiritism. It is divided into four parts: “Primary Causes”; “The Spiritual World or Spirits”; “Moral Laws”; and “Hope and Consolation”. It is composed of 1,018 questions asked by Kardec to the superior Spirits responsible for the arrival of Spiritism among men. What is God? Where do we come from? Where are we going? What are we doing on Earth? These are some of the questions answered by the phalanx of the Spirit of Truth.
The Mediums’ Book
Its publication was in 1861. Allan Kardec shows the benefits and dangers of mediumship, that is, the link that connects the incarnate man to the spiritual world. He demonstrates that while all living beings have this opening of contact, there are those in whom it is much more accentuated. Kardec and the Superior Spirits warn about the subtlety of this faculty so that a person can contact Spirits without being disturbed by entities of evil, thus losing control of their mediumship.
The Gospel According to Spiritism
Published in 1864, this work can be considered the moral part of spiritist philosophy. Kardec and the Superior Spirits comment on the main passages of Jesus’ life, in accessible language. They explain his parables and demonstrate the greatness of the Master in his teachings, in addition to giving us important advice on our daily conduct in the face of life’s difficulties and doubts about them.
Heaven and Hell
Kardec published this book in 1865. Through the invocation of the Spirits of people from different social classes, beliefs and behaviors, he shows us what their arrival and life in the spiritual world was like after their disincarnation. Queens, peasants, nuns, murderers, ignorant and intellectuals are some of those who tell what awaited them after their earthly attitudes and how their future life could be.
Genesis
In this 1868 work, Kardec explains Biblical Genesis, the formation of the Universe, demonstrating its consistency when faced with scientific knowledge devoid of allegories proper to the time in which it was written. He exposes what miracles are, explained by the laws of nature, produced by the modification of the fluids that surround us. Finally, he makes religion and science work together, strengthening the faith of those who believe in God.

content:
Most spiritist centers began with simple study meetings held in family homes, with the participation of relatives and friends. It was from this union and harmony of ideas that many spiritist centers were founded throughout the world. It was no different for the Spiritist Study Center Fraternity. After a period of gatherings of a group of friends that took place every week around a table in the living room of a small apartment, the moment came when they decided to found a spiritist center. The main ideal of this group at that time, and which remains so today, was to promote Spiritism in Montreal, in order to bring to Québécois and immigrants the message of love and charity of spiritist philosophy. Founded on August 9, 2005, CESF began operating at 797 Gordon Street, in Verdun, Montreal, in facilities donated by the couple Roberto Lavoie and Isabelle Norris, active members of the center’s work.
Subsequently, the founding group developed the Bylaws and established a Board of Directors to oversee the center’s activities, which was thus constituted under the name “Spiritist Study Center Fraternity”. On March 23, 2006, the center received its letters patent - Societies Act, Part III, registration number 1163604623. Obtaining this document was necessary to regularize CESF’s status as a legally constituted, non-profit entity. At that time, all Tuesdays and Wednesdays held study meetings; on Fridays, mediumistic meetings and mediumship development and education courses; and on Saturdays, study meetings of the Book of Spirits and the Gospel According to Spiritism.
By 2007, already 40 people attended the center every week and activities were conducted from Tuesday to Saturday. By 2010, activities took place at the center from Monday to Saturday; about 60 people attended each week and about 150 people were directly or indirectly connected to the center. Due to the growing number of people attending the center, our facilities became too cramped and therefore inadequate for the proper continuation of activities. The Board of Directors therefore decided to seek new facilities.
On August 20, 2011, CESF moved and our headquarters is now located at 5573 Verdun Street, Montreal. Thus, CESF, which initially began its activities around a table in the living room of a small apartment, now occupies an area of 2,400 square meters, with conference and meeting rooms for more than 100 people, study rooms and mediumistic meetings, a passage room, a library, and administrative offices. There is also a basement of the same area as the ground floor dedicated to moral education activities for children and adolescents. With the comfort of a larger space adapted to our needs, CESF now offers members and those who attend the center daily activities from Monday to Saturday.

content:
God is the supreme intelligence, the first cause of all things. He is eternal, immutable, immaterial, unique, all-powerful, supremely just and good.
God created the universe, which includes all rational and irrational beings, animate and inanimate, material and immaterial.
Beyond the corporeal world, where incarnate Spirits who are men live, there exists a spiritual world, the home of disembodied Spirits.
In the universe, there are other worlds inhabited by beings at different levels of evolution: equal, more evolved, or less evolved than men.
All the laws of nature are divine laws, since God is their author. They encompass physical and moral laws.
Man is a Spirit embodied in a material body. The perispirit is the semi-material body that unites the Spirit to the material body.
Spirits are the intelligent beings of creation. They constitute the spiritual world, which pre-exists and survives all things.
Spirits are created simple and ignorant. They evolve intellectually and morally, passing from a lower order to a higher order, toward perfection, where they enjoy unalterable happiness.
Spirits preserve their individuality before, during, and after each incarnation.
Spirits reincarnate as many times as necessary for their own perfection.
Spirits are in constant evolution. In their multiple corporeal existences, they may remain stationary, but never regress. The speed of their intellectual and moral progress depends on their efforts to achieve perfection.
Spirits are of different orders, depending on the degree of perfection they have achieved: pure Spirits, who have achieved the highest degree of perfection; good spirits, in whom the desire for good predominates; imperfect Spirits, characterized by ignorance, desire for evil, and inferior passions.
Relations between Spirits and men are constant and have always existed. Good Spirits call us to do good, support us in life’s trials, and help us bear them with courage and resignation. Wicked spirits deceive us.
Jesus is the guide and model of all Humanity. And the philosophy that he taught and practiced is the purest expression of God’s Law.
The morality of Christ, contained in the Gospel, is the path to follow for the safe evolution of all men, and its practice is the solution to all human problems, as well as the goal to be achieved by Humanity.
Man has free will to act, but is responsible for the consequences of his actions.
The future life reserves for men pains and pleasures compatible with their behavior in accordance with or against God’s Law.
Prayer is an act of worshipping God. It is in natural law and results from an innate feeling in man, just as the idea of the Creator’s existence is innate.
Prayer makes man better. He who prays with fervor and confidence is stronger against the temptations of evil, and God sends him good Spirits to help him. It is help that is never denied him when asked with sincerity.
Source: adapted text, Brazilian Spiritist Federation - FEB

content:
Spiritism is in itself only a philosophical doctrine built on exact facts and natural laws still unknown; in its essence, this doctrine, by profoundly modifying ideas, touches all social questions and, consequently, the religious question, like all others. Don’t all philosophies deal with this? Since they comment on the foundations of all religions, that is, God, the origin and nature of the soul? Doesn’t materialist philosophy also concern itself with this from the point of view of negation? It is even impossible for a philosophy not to deal with these questions in one direction or another. Spiritism could therefore deal with it in parallel with the help of the new elements that precede it; but that is not what constitutes a religion, otherwise all philosophies would be religions.
We must distinguish the religious idea from religion properly speaking. The religious idea is general, without the principle of fixed details, without any regulation. Religion has a particular character of precision that consists not only of a community of well-defined beliefs, but in the external form of worship, in the fulfillment of certain duties, and in the bond that unites adherents. This is what spiritualism never had, which is why it was not a religion. One is a spiritualist because one sympathizes with the idea it contains, as one is Cartesian, Platonic, spiritualist or materialist, but not by a profession of faith or any consecration.
Spiritism has no dogmas, cults, rites, ceremonies or hierarchies; it neither asks nor admits any blind faith; it wants to see everything clearly; it wants us to understand everything, to perceive everything.
In the philosophical sense, spiritualism is a religion because it is the doctrine that founds the bonds of fraternity and communion of thoughts on a simple convention, but on more solid bases, the very laws of matter. Why then do we declare that spiritualism is not a religion? Because there is only one word to express two different ideas and that, in general opinion, the word religion is inseparable from the word cult, which exclusively awakens an idea of form and that spiritualism does not have. We vehemently reject the dogmas that crystallize research and often oppose reason, as well as the rites that tend to give usurped power to those who practice them.

content:
From Leon Denis, in the book: In the Invisible
All manifestations of nature and life can be summarized in vibrations, more or less rapid and extensive, according to the causes that produce them. Everything vibrates in the universe: sound, light, heat, electricity, magnetism, chemical rays, cathode rays, radio waves, etc., are only the various modes of undulation, vibration of universal force and substance, the successive degrees that constitute, as a whole, the ascending scale of energy manifestations.
These degrees are very far apart from each other. Sound travels 340 meters per second; light, in the same time, crosses 300,000 kilometers; electricity is propagated with a speed that seems incalculable to us. But our physical senses do not allow us to perceive all modes of vibration. Their inability to give us a complete impression of nature’s forces is a well-known fact that we do not need to insist on further.
Only in the field of optics do we know that light waves only impress our retina within the limits of the seven colors of the prism, from red to purple. Beyond or below these colors, solar radiations escape our sight; they are then called dark rays.
Between the limit of sounds, whose vibrations are 24 to 60,000 per second, and the sensation of heat, which is measured by trillions of vibrations, we perceive nothing. It is the same between the sensation of heat and that of light, which corresponds, on average, to 500 trillion vibrations per second.
In this stupendous ascent, our senses represent widely spaced floors, stations placed at considerable distances from each other on an endless road. Between these various stages, for example, between high-pitched sounds and the phenomena of heat and light, from there to the vibrational zones affected by cathode rays, there are for us as chasms. But would not these chasms, apparently empty and obscure, be filled by beings endowed with senses more subtle or more numerous than ours? Between the vibrations perceived by hearing and those that impress our vision, is there nothing but emptiness in the domain of forces and universal life?
It would make little sense to believe so, because everything in nature follows, is connected and unfolds, from one ring to another, through gradual transitions. Nowhere is there a sudden jump, void, hiatus. What emerges from these considerations is simply the insufficiency of our organism, too poor to perceive all modes of energy.
What we say about the forces in action in the universe also applies to all beings and things, in their various forms, at their various degrees of condensation or rarefaction.
Our knowledge of the universe is restricted or expanded, depending on the number and subtlety of our senses. Our present organism only allows us to embrace a very limited circle of the empire of things. Many forms of life escape us. But let a new sense be added to our senses, and immediately the invisible is revealed, the emptiness is populated, dark insensitivity gains life.

content:
Is Spiritism a science?
By Charles Kempf
The words spiritualism and spiritualist have a very general meaning: anyone who thinks there is something different from matter in them is a spiritualist. On the other hand, the terms SPIRITISM and SPIRITIST are neologisms, that is, words invented by its codifier, Allan Kardec.
Allan Kardec defines Spiritism as “a science that deals with the nature, origin and destiny of Spirits and their relationship with the corporeal world.” Spiritism is therefore well defined as science. But it differs from scientific disciplines already established and studied in academies by the object of its studies: the spiritual element.
To illustrate this point, we will first try to identify, in a brief historical summary, the elements that characterize Spiritism.
Next, we will draw a parallel with some classical and modern concepts of science, to show the links and differences in relation to Spiritism. Finally, we will discuss the various aspects of knowledge.

content:
All spiritualist practice is free, according to the Gospel principle: “Give freely what you have received freely”.
Spiritualist practice has no external worship, according to the Christian principle that God should be worshipped in spirit and in truth.
Spiritism has no priesthood, gurus, and the like. It does not adopt or use in its meetings and practices: facings, alcoholic beverages, incense, smoke, altars, icons, stretchers, candles, processions, talismans, amulets, sacraments, granting of indulgences, horoscopes, divination, pyramids, crystals, seashells, rituals, or any other form of external worship.
Spiritism does not impose its principles. It invites those who wish to know it to submit its teachings to the test of reason before accepting them.
Mediumship, which enables communication between Spirits and men, is a gift that many people bring at birth, regardless of the doctrinal line adopted in their life.
Spiritist mediumnic practice is only that which is exercised on the basis of the principles of Spiritist Doctrine and according to Christian morality.

content:
Spiritist centers are frequently sought by people who need help to resolve a variety of personal problems. Some people cannot overcome the loss of a loved one; others suffer and suffer from depression; many others seek to understand the meaning of their lives, are depressed and hopeless, and still others have physical problems whose causes have not been found.
CESF maintains a free spiritual assistance service to listen to these people with attention and seek to help them according to spiritist philosophy. By attempting to discover the main reasons for their problems, we end up relieving them. Many situations of this nature can be better understood by applying the spiritualist teaching that “every effect has a cause” and, therefore, when it is found, problems can be overcome.
It is important to note that these interviews are conducted by people experienced and familiar with spiritist philosophy and the means that Spiritism offers to help them. In these cases, we ask interested parties to contact us to schedule an appointment. Click on CONTACT and we will get back to you.
